editorial.headline: Self-Service Food Retail: National Limits and Bali’s Closed Door
editorial.standfirst: This code covers self-service retail led by food, beverages or tobacco, yet its national foreign-ownership ceiling is 0% and Bali expressly closes it to PMA.
editorial.body:
This activity is the self-service retailing of a broad mix of everyday goods in which food ingredients, prepared food, beverages or tobacco remain the dominant offer. Prices are set in advance; customers select items themselves and pay at a cashier. The format may also sell selected non-food items—household furnishings, children’s toys, medicines, medical devices and clothing—but these do not alter the central character of the business: food, beverages or tobacco lead the assortment. Hypermarkets and supermarkets are expressly within its scope.

The code is open across the full business-scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because scale does not dilute the operating identity. Whether the enterprise is small or large, it remains a self-service retailer whose principal merchandise is food, beverages or tobacco, with any permitted non-food range remaining secondary to that retail core.

Nationally, the PMA position is limited, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. In practical terms, the record does not present this as a route for foreign equity participation. The applicable national reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. A registration decision should therefore begin with the actual retail model—self-service checkout, predetermined prices and a food-, beverage- or tobacco-led range—rather than with the presence of ancillary household or consumer goods on the shelves.

Bali is more direct still. The provincial status is closed, and the stated reason is that minimarkets and supermarkets are reserved for Indonesian citizens and closed to PMA. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today through PMA. Bali also maintains an island-wide, permanent block on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities; the record identifies that provincial rule separately. The essential conclusion is not a matter of branding or store size: this self-service retail activity is nationally limited to a 0% foreign-ownership ceiling and expressly closed to PMA in Bali.
